name: o3de-development-tools
description: Developer companion for Open 3D Engine (O3DE): guided workspace setup, one-click CMake build & run, and C++ IntelliSense — for VS Code on Windows and Linux.
author: Genome Studios Inc

o3de.enabled.markdownDescription: **Enable O3DE Tools for this project.** Per-project opt-in: the extension's automatic behavior (C++/Lua IntelliSense, the run-state watcher, MCP auto-start) runs only in projects where this is `true`. Stored per folder in `.vscode/settings.json`, so a non-O3DE workspace (e.g. web development) is never affected. Set it from the one-time prompt, the Onboarding ▸ Required row, or **O3DE: Enable Tools for this Project**.

o3de.intellisense.autoRefreshOnStartup.markdownDescription: On activation, regenerate C++ IntelliSense (`c_cpp_properties.json`) from the latest CMake File API reply. Low cost — re-parses the existing reply, does **not** run a CMake configure. Turn off to update only via the **O3DE: Generate C++ IntelliSense** command.

o3de.run.toggleToQuit.markdownDescription: Make **O3DE: Run** (and its `Ctrl+Alt+R` hotkey) a toggle: when an O3DE app is already running, pressing Run **force-quits** it instead of trying to launch a second one (the Editor can't run twice) — one key to launch on demand and quit on demand. Turn **off** to make Run only ever launch (it will offer to restart if something is already running).

o3de.cmake.configureArgs.markdownDescription: Extra CMake **cache variables** passed to **O3DE: Configure Project** as `-D<name>=<value>` (e.g. `LY_RENDERDOC_ENABLED: "ON"`, `CMAKE_OBJECT_PATH_MAX: "1000"`). Managed by the **Advanced** tab, but editable here. Changes apply on the next Configure (CMake caches them in `CMakeCache.txt`).

o3de.llm.enabled.markdownDescription: **Allow LLM connections.** Expose a local [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) endpoint on `127.0.0.1` so an assistant like Claude can trigger builds and read back structured results — no rebuilt scripts. **Off by default**; the endpoint binds to localhost only. Per-project (stored in `.vscode/settings.json`) so enabling it on one project does not affect others. Run **O3DE: Show LLM Connection Info** for the client config. Toggle from the Onboarding ▸ Optional section.

o3de.llm.port.markdownDescription: TCP port for the local LLM (MCP) endpoint on `127.0.0.1` (only used when `#o3de.llm.enabled#` is on). **`0` = auto:** derive a **stable per-project port** so multiple VS Code windows (one per O3DE project) each get their own endpoint and never collide — the port stays the same across reloads, so each project's pasted `.mcp.json` keeps working. Set a specific number to pin the port for this project. Run **O3DE: Show LLM Connection Info** to see the resolved port.

o3de.llm.requireToken.markdownDescription: Require a bearer token on the LLM (MCP) endpoint. **Off by default** — the endpoint is bound to `127.0.0.1` (local only), and some MCP clients mishandle a token by falling into an OAuth flow. Turn on only if you want the extra gate and your client sends the `Authorization` header from its config.

o3de.llm.allowForceClose.markdownDescription: Expose the destructive **`o3de_force_close`** MCP tool, which lets an assistant force-quit the running Editor / GameLauncher / AssetProcessor (e.g. to unblock a build that a running Editor is holding gem DLLs for). **Off by default** so the assistant can never close your Editor unless you opt in — and even when on, the tool is marked *destructive* so your client asks for approval before every call. Leave off to keep force-close a manual action (the O3DE panel's Stop).

o3de.llm.writeMcpConfig.markdownDescription: When LLM connections are enabled, automatically write/merge the `o3de` server entry into your project's `.mcp.json` (created if absent, other servers preserved) so a client like Claude Code finds it with no copy-paste. Disabling LLM connections removes the entry again. Turn this off to manage `.mcp.json` yourself (use **O3DE: Show LLM Connection Info** to copy the block).

o3de.linuxSupport.markdownDescription: **Enable the Linux build/run/debug paths.** On by default — O3DE Development Tools supports Windows and Linux. On Linux the toolchain is gcc/clang + Ninja Multi-Config (no MSVC), inherited from your shell. Turn this **off** to make O3DE build/configure/run stand down on Linux, which is only useful as an escape hatch if the Linux paths misbehave on your machine. Per-project (stored in `.vscode/settings.json`). Use **O3DE: Copy Environment Report** when filing a Linux bug so the report is self-diagnosing.

o3de.experimental.linuxSupport.markdownDeprecationMessage: **Deprecated** — Linux support is no longer experimental and is on by default. Use `o3de.linuxSupport` instead; this key is still honoured so an existing setting keeps working.
